note: Gates the gate: it MUST return verified-good on a load-bearing suite, verified-bad on a decorative one, UNVERIFIABLE when a mutant dies unobserved, UNVERIFIABLE on an empty inventory, and it MUST execute the bytes it wrote rather than a previous mutant's cached bytecode. `check` READS this file — inverting any expectation here reds the suite.

vectors.name: crashing
vectors.note: CRASH != KILLED. A mutant that dies without the declared kill_witness was not observed by any assertion. Regression control for bin/recompute-mutation-survival:73.

vectors.name: stale-bytecode
vectors.note: EXECUTION FRESHNESS control. Both mutants are same-byte-length edits to one file, so the source size never changes; the test command additionally stamps a fixed mtime, so mtime cannot discriminate either. CPython validates timestamp .pyc on (mtime, size), so without per-run isolation every run reuses the baseline's bytecode and BOTH mutants are misread. Pinning both rows is deliberate: pinning only the survivor would let a run that got the first mutant wrong still pass. Remove the Workspace isolation and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-12.)

vectors.name: zero-mutants
vectors.note: An empty inventory certified coverage: killed 0 / survived 0 read as verified-good / exit 0. Same class as #65 ZERO_MUTANTS, but it has to be guarded at this tool's own boundary because #66 discovers suites by mutation_check.py and this suite has none. Remove the guard and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-12.)

vectors.name: not-applied
vectors.note: A mutation whose anchor is absent was never applied, so the run says nothing about the suite — grading it either way would be fabricating evidence. Presence is not application: testing with `in` and applying with replace(..., 1) mutates the first occurrence, which need not be the site `must` refers to. Witnesses the applied-exactly-once precondition, which until now no vector reached.

vectors.name: red-baseline
vectors.note: The suite fails before any mutation, so no later failure can be attributed to a mutant: every mutation would score as KILLED by a failure it did not cause. UNVERIFIABLE before the first mutant is applied. Witnesses the baseline-green precondition, which until now no vector reached.

vectors.name: all-probe
vectors.note: Only a `guard` gates the verdict, so an inventory of probes alone certifies nothing — the first cut of the guard tested an empty list and this walked straight past it, returning verified-good / exit 0 with a decorative test and the probe surviving. `ZERO_MUTANTS` with reason `no_guard_mutations`. Remove the guard and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-13.)

vectors.name: stale-copy
vectors.note: The suite imports a vendored COPY and never loads the mutated file, so the mutant survives trivially. SURVIVED would assert a gap in the suite's ASSERTIONS; the real finding is that it never read the file — and this test WOULD kill the mutant if it saw it. Per-run isolation cannot catch this because the copy travels with the workspace; the observation control can. Remove the observation control and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-13.)

vectors.name: refutation-outranks
vectors.note: A SURVIVED guard is a PROVEN coverage gap; an UNVERIFIABLE row is the absence of a result. Absence must not outrank evidence — this previously reported UNVERIFIABLE / exit 2 while printing the survivor below it, so the machine-readable answer hid a refutation the run had established. Both rows pinned, because pinning only one lets the other regress unseen. (zexoverz, 2026-10-13.)
